# routeros_mpls_ldp_advertise_filter (Resource)


## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "routeros_mpls_ldp_advertise_filter" "filter" {
  advertise = true
  comment   = "Managed by OpenTofu"
  disabled  = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `___id___` (Number) <em>Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___path___` (String) <em>Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___skip___` (String) <em>A set of transformations for field names. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `advertise` (Boolean) Whether to advertise the label mappings matched by this rule.
- `comment` (String)
- `disabled` (Boolean)
- `neighbor` (String) Neighbor the label mapping would be advertised to, written as an IPv4/IPv6 address or as an `address/prefix` range. An empty value matches every neighbor.
- `place_before` (String) Before which position the rule will be inserted.  
	> Please check the effect of this option, as it does not work as you think!  
	> Best way to use in conjunction with a data source. See [example](../data-sources/ip_firewall.md#example-usage).
- `prefix` (String) Prefix of the label mapping to match, written as `address/prefix-length`. An empty value matches every prefix.
- `vrf` (String) Name of the VRF this rule applies to. The special value `any` applies the rule to every VRF.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import
Import is supported using the following syntax:
```shell
#The ID can be found via API or the terminal
#The command for the terminal is -> :put [/mpls/ldp/advertise-filter get [print show-ids]]
terraform import routeros_mpls_ldp_advertise_filter.filter "*1"
```
